newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: AMBASSADOR TO IRAN RECALLED
Australia is recalling its Ambassador to Iran immediately following a German court finding that Iran was directly responsible for acts of terrorism.
Ambassador Stuart Hume is being brought back to Australia for consultations and briefings about the German case.
The German court has found Iran's leadership was directly responsible for the murders of four Iranian Kurds in Berlin in 1992.
Australia has previously refused to act against Iran, stating there was no direct evidence linking the Iranian Government to terrorist acts.
A spokesman for Australian Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer, says the verdict in the case implicates the highest level of the Iranain state in the killings.
Mr Downer's office says Australia utterly condemns all acts of terrorism.
OPPOSITION SAYS CUTS WILL AFFECT DEFENCE STAFF MORALE
The Federal Opposition says the radical cuts to Defence Force staff will only shatter an already low morale in defence.
Defence Minister, Ian McLachlan, announced a program to cut eight thousand defence jobs.
Mr McLachlan says he'll cut 15-percent of defence public servants and eight percent of full time military, with the savings of up to one-billion dollars annually to go towards combat areas.
Mr McLachlan released a defence review which said the strategic outlook for Australia's region is more complex, uncertain and demanding.
WOOLDRIDGE SAYS NOT ALL FUNDS WILL DROP PALLIATIVE CARE
Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge predicts no health fund will completely drop coverage of palliative care, even though the Productivity Commission recommends they do so.
Dr Wooldridge said it's not fair that all Australians who take out private health cover should be forced to pay for palliative care.
He says at the moment Funds can get out of palliative care if they want to because of the way the legislation is framed.
Dr Wooldridge says the Government is doing things to help Funds because it wants to help the 33 per cent of the population who are their members.
EMOTIONAL FAREWELL FOR MURDER VICTIM

More than 15-hundred people today packed Perth's Saint Mary's Cathedral for the funeral of murder victim Ciara Glennon. Ms Glennon's body was found in bush, north of Perth, last week, 20 days after she disappeared from the Claremont nightstrip.
Mourners included members of Perth's Irish community, Ms Glennon's work colleagues, students from her high school, the business fraternity, politicians and police.
Her father, Dennis Glennon broke down as he delivered an emotional eulogy.
STONE WANTS TRIBUNAL DISBANDED
Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone has stepped up his attack on the Native Title process calling for the Native Title Tribunal to be disbanded.
Mr Stone has told a pastoralists' meeting in Alice Springs, the belief native title and pastoral leases can co-exist is nonsense.

He's called for the Federal Government to extinguish Native Title on pastoral leases as a first step, and to remove the right of native title-holders' to negotiate, describing that right as akin to blackmail.

Mr Stone also wants a sunset clause on all claims no later than the year 2001, powers under the Native Title Act vested in state and territory jurisdictions, and the commonwealth to meet all compensation claims.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
